user_selected_source.complete_text:
Students are fleeing computer science.

US enrollment in computer and information science programs fell more than 12% for undergraduates and more than 10% for graduate students this fall, per preliminary data from the National Student Clearinghouse.

Over two years, undergraduate enrollment is down 18.4% and graduate enrollment 27.1%, reversing years of growth as AI cuts into entry-level coding jobs.

The initial successful FxTwitter full-note response also had no attached media. No replies, profile images, invented chart or unrelated media were used.

primary_sources.title: Clearinghouse Enrollment Insights Series: Preliminary Fall Enrollment Trends
primary_sources.verified_excerpt: Enrollment in Computer and Information Science programs continues to decline sharply, with double-digit decreases across institutions (-12.4% at 4-years, -12.3% at 2-years, and -10.4% at graduate institutions).
primary_sources.additional_scope_excerpt: The estimates provided in this report are preliminary and subject to revision.

primary_sources.title: 5 Highlights from the Preliminary Fall Enrollment Trends Report
primary_sources.verified_excerpt: Computer and Information Science undergraduate enrollment is declining at both 4-year and 2-year institutions, decreasing by 12.4 percent and 12.3 percent, respectively. Graduate enrollment is also declining by 10.4 percent.
primary_sources.final_report_timing: The Research Center will release its Final Fall Enrollment Trends report in January 2027.

primary_sources.title: Preliminary Fall Enrollment Trends: Fall 2026 — Methodological Notes
primary_sources.verified_excerpt: The current report reflects approximately 7.92 million enrollments reported as of September 24, 2026, by 46.0 percent of postsecondary institutions in the U.S. that are participating in the Clearinghouse.

reporting_scope.measure: Year-over-year percentage change in enrollment within the reporting institution panel
reporting_scope.methodology: Unweighted enrollment counts from a fixed panel of institutions consistently reporting fall data within the comparable submission window in 2024, 2025 and 2026. Percentage-change analysis controls institutional coverage and submission timing; final report uses different methodology and expanded coverage.

all_field_report_coverage.coverage_note: Institution and enrollment coverage use fall 2025 submissions as denominator; these figures describe the overall report, not only computing programs.

editorial_limits: Keep Computer and Information Sciences visible; do not silently broaden the declines to all students or all majors.
Keep undergraduate institutional levels distinct from graduate enrollment.
Show preliminary and Fall 2026 versus Fall 2025; distinguish these term comparisons from the November 16 edition date.
Enrollment changes are not evidence that the same percentage of students dropped out or fled; transitions, new entrants and completions all affect enrollment.
The post connects enrollment to AI and entry-level coding jobs, but these sources do not establish that causal claim. Do not author it as a measured conclusion.
The post two-year claims of -18.4% undergraduate and -27.1% graduate enrollment were not independently verified against the underlying dashboard and are omitted from the planned graphic.
No chart is attached to the selected post; use clearly labeled statistic panels if useful, without inventing an original source chart.
recommended_source_line: Source: National Student Clearinghouse Research Center; post: @unusual_whales, Nov. 15, 2026.
